AgentCore Description: Converts APIs / Lambda / OpenAPI / Smithy specs into MCP-compatible tools served through a unified Gateway endpoint. Supports 1-click connectors for Salesforce / Slack / Jira / Asana / Zendesk.
TrueFoundry Description: Centralized gateway that sits between agents and all registered MCP servers. Routes tool calls with RBAC and auth enforcement. Supports OpenAPI-to-MCP conversion for wrapping REST APIs.
Integration Recommendation: Pick one as the MCP control plane. TrueFoundry preferred for multi-framework governance; AgentCore preferred for AWS-native Lambda-backed tooling.

AgentCore Description: Built-in hybrid semantic + keyword search over all registered tools so agents can find the right tool without exhaustive enumeration.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry MCP Registry supports semantic and keyword search over registered MCP servers and tools.
Integration Recommendation: Functional equivalents — both solve the N×M tool discovery problem. If using TrueFoundry as the MCP layer avoid running both in parallel.

AgentCore Description: Gateway combines multiple APIs / Lambdas / functions into a single MCP endpoint.
TrueFoundry Description: Compose curated subsets of tools from multiple MCP servers into a single endpoint for scoped agent access.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry Virtual MCP Servers are the stronger pattern for multi-tenant or role-scoped tool slices; AgentCore is simpler for single-account AWS setups.

AgentCore Description: Import an OpenAPI or Smithy spec and AgentCore Gateway auto-generates MCP tools.
TrueFoundry Description: Wraps existing REST APIs as MCP servers without rewriting code.
Integration Recommendation: Identical intent. Use whichever gateway owns the MCP control plane in your architecture.

AgentCore Description: Pre-built connectors for Salesforce / Slack / Jira / Asana / Zendesk with auth pre-wired.
TrueFoundry Description: Pre-built MCP servers for Slack / Confluence / Sentry / Datadog and others.
Integration Recommendation: Different catalog coverage. AgentCore has CRM/PM SaaS; TrueFoundry leans DevOps/monitoring. Complement rather than duplicate.

AgentCore Description: Gateway enforces inbound auth — verifies agent identity before tool access. Supports JWT from corporate IdPs (Cognito / Okta / Azure Entra ID / Auth0).
TrueFoundry Equivalent: Centralized MCP Auth — One API Key
TrueFoundry Description: One API key (or JWT) reaches every registered MCP server. Auto-refreshed OAuth 2.0 tokens per user across all servers.
Integration Recommendation: Both solve inbound auth to the gateway control plane. Running both in parallel creates redundant auth checks on the same request path — pick one.

AgentCore Feature: Outbound Credential Exchange (OAuth / API Keys per tool)
AgentCore Description: AgentCore Identity manages per-tool outbound auth — injects credentials so agents call third-party services without holding secrets.
TrueFoundry Description: Unified OAuth 2.0 token management with automatic token refresh across all MCP servers — one token per user.
Integration Recommendation: Direct overlap. Both handle "the agent shouldn't hold credentials itself." Consolidate into the chosen gateway layer.

AgentCore Feature: IdP Integration (Cognito / Okta / Azure Entra / Auth0)
AgentCore Description: AgentCore Identity integrates with external IdPs for workload identity issuance. Supports private IdPs via VPC.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry AI Gateway supports OIDC / SAML SSO with YAML-based RBAC policies scoped per user / team / service account.
Integration Recommendation: Different granularity: AgentCore creates per-agent workload identities; TrueFoundry enforces org-level RBAC. Both are needed — use together without conflict.

AgentCore Description: Agent identities are issued as workload identities (IAM-compatible) with agent-specific attributes and capability flags.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry supports scoped service accounts and API keys per application or team for machine-to-machine access.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore workload identities are finer-grained (per-agent token); TrueFoundry service accounts are broader (per-team or per-app). Use AgentCore Identity for agent-level tokens; TrueFoundry RBAC for team-level gating.

AgentCore Description: Authors deterministic Cedar policies from natural language. Intercepts every tool call via Gateway before execution. Includes NL-to-Cedar translation with safety validation.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry supports Cedar policy language for fine-grained access control on MCP tool invocations (Pre-Tool hook). Also supports OPA-based policies.
Integration Recommendation: Both use Cedar as the policy engine. Risk of double policy evaluation on the same tool call. Consolidate into one — if TrueFoundry owns the MCP gateway use its Cedar guardrails; do not run AgentCore Policy on top.

AgentCore Feature: Fine-Grained Tool Access Controls (user identity + input params)
AgentCore Description: AgentCore Policy supports conditions based on caller identity AND tool input parameter values — not just coarse allow/deny.
TrueFoundry Equivalent: RBAC per Tool / Operation (Granular MCP Controls)
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry supports granular RBAC: control which teams and roles can access which tools and specific operations within a server.
Integration Recommendation: Both do attribute-based access. AgentCore supports parameter-level conditions (e.g. "allow DELETE only if record.owner == caller"); TrueFoundry RBAC is operation-level (allow/deny a tool). For HIPAA rule enforcement AgentCore's param-level conditions add depth.

AgentCore Description: Every policy evaluation decision is logged to CloudWatch with metrics on allow/deny counts.
TrueFoundry Description: Full request-level tracing and audit logs for every tool invocation including policy outcomes.
Integration Recommendation: Both emit policy audit logs. AgentCore logs to CloudWatch; TrueFoundry logs to its own observability stack (exportable to S3 / custom storage). Pick one system of record to avoid duplicate audit trails.

AgentCore Description: Not native in AgentCore — Cedar is the primary policy language.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry supports Open Policy Agent (OPA) alongside Cedar for full policy lifecycle management including Rego policies.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore does not support OPA natively. TrueFoundry OPA guardrails are complementary — run them in TrueFoundry's MCP layer without conflict.

AgentCore Description: End-to-end trace visualization of agent reasoning steps / tool invocations / model interactions via CloudWatch dashboards. OTEL-compatible telemetry.
TrueFoundry Description: OpenTelemetry-compliant traces / spans / logs exported to TrueFoundry dashboards. Token usage / cost / latency / error rate per request. Exportable to S3 or custom storage.
Integration Recommendation: Direct overlap. Both consume OTEL telemetry and produce trace visualizations. Do NOT run both concurrently on the same agent session — double ingestion = double cost + split traces.

AgentCore Description: Built-in CloudWatch dashboards for session count / latency / token usage / error rates. Cross-account observability supported.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry AI Gateway provides dashboards for per-model / per-team / per-user cost attribution / latency / token spend / error rates.
Integration Recommendation: Feature-equivalent. TrueFoundry's cost attribution (per-team / per-model) is stronger for chargeback scenarios; CloudWatch is richer for AWS infra correlation. Run one for AI-layer telemetry; use CloudWatch only for infra metrics.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Observability can mask PII in logs and spans.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry's built-in PII/PHI guardrail detects and redacts PII from LLM inputs and outputs (Azure AI Language powered). HIPAA-relevant.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore masks PII in telemetry; TrueFoundry redacts PII from the actual LLM payloads before they reach the model. Complementary — both needed for HIPAA compliance. Not duplicate.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore emits span logs ($0.35/GB) and event logs ($0.50/GB) to CloudWatch Logs.
TrueFoundry Equivalent: Request and Response Logging with Metadata Tagging
TrueFoundry Description: Full request/response logs tagged by user ID / team / environment / model. Retention and export configurable per plan.
Integration Recommendation: Parallel logging of the same AI traffic. Consolidate to TrueFoundry's logging (which stays in your storage) for AI-layer logs; reserve CloudWatch for AgentCore Runtime infrastructure logs.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Observability supports routing telemetry across AWS accounts for multi-account enterprise setups.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry can be deployed per-VPC or on-prem for data residency; does not natively federate across cloud accounts.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore advantage for multi-AWS-account enterprise architectures. TrueFoundry does not have a native cross-account federation story.

AgentCore Description: Intercepts tool calls at the Gateway and enforces Cedar policies before tool execution. Supports NL-to-Cedar authoring.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry supports pre-call and post-call guardrail hooks on every MCP tool invocation — Cedar / OPA / SQL sanitizer / secrets detection / code safety linter.
Integration Recommendation: Both sit on the tool invocation path. TrueFoundry's MCP guardrail set is richer (code safety / SQL sanitizer / secrets detection). If TrueFoundry owns the MCP layer use its guardrail hooks and skip AgentCore Policy — they do the same interception.

AgentCore Feature: AgentCore has no built-in LLM content moderation guardrails
AgentCore Description: AgentCore Policy is Cedar-based tool authorization — not content moderation for LLM inputs/outputs.
TrueFoundry Equivalent: LLM Input/Output Guardrails (PII / Content Moderation / Prompt Injection / Hallucination)
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry AI Gateway intercepts LLM prompts AND responses. Input: PII/PHI detection + redaction / prompt injection / content moderation. Output: hallucination detection / secrets detection / content filtering.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry provides LLM-layer content safety that AgentCore does not have. Fully complementary — run TrueFoundry guardrails on LLM calls regardless of which gateway handles tools.

AgentCore Description: N/A — AgentCore has no SQL sanitizer.
TrueFoundry Description: Catches and blocks risky SQL patterns (DROP / TRUNCATE / DELETE without WHERE / string interpolation) in tool arguments.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry-only feature. Critical for healthcare member-data query agents.

AgentCore Description: N/A — AgentCore has no secrets detection guardrail.
TrueFoundry Description: Catches and redacts credentials (AWS keys / API keys / JWT tokens / private keys) in LLM outputs or MCP tool results.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry-only. Run in TrueFoundry's output guardrail layer for all agent responses — no AgentCore equivalent.

AgentCore Description: N/A
TrueFoundry Description: Flags unsafe code patterns (eval / exec / os.system / subprocess / dangerous shell commands) in code generated by agents.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry-only. Relevant for code-generation agents (claims adjudication automation / FWA detection pipelines).

AgentCore Feature: AgentCore is not an LLM router — it runs agents and tools; model access is direct Bedrock or provider API
AgentCore Description: AgentCore Harness supports Amazon Bedrock / OpenAI / Google Gemini / any OpenAI-compatible model. No unified routing / caching / fallback abstraction.
TrueFoundry Equivalent: Unified LLM API (1000+ LLMs) — Load Balancing / Fallback / Routing
TrueFoundry Description: Single OpenAI-compatible endpoint for 1000+ LLMs. Weight-based / latency-based / priority routing. Automatic fallback chains and retries across providers.
Integration Recommendation: Non-overlapping. TrueFoundry's AI Gateway handles LLM routing; AgentCore runs on top of whatever model it calls. Run TrueFoundry as the LLM proxy — AgentCore agents point to TrueFoundry's endpoint.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore has no caching layer.
TrueFoundry Description: Exact and semantic caching of LLM responses to reduce costs and latency on repeated or similar prompts.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry-only. Layer over all AgentCore LLM calls to cut token costs — compatible.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore has no rate limiting for LLM calls.
TrueFoundry Description: Per-user / per-model / per-application token and request-count throttles configurable via YAML.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry-only at the LLM call layer. AgentCore has no built-in LLM rate limiting. Use TrueFoundry to enforce HIPAA-grade access controls on model usage.

AgentCore Description: N/A
TrueFoundry Description: Enforce dollar-amount spend limits per team or user. Real-time cost attribution with alerts.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry-only. Critical for multi-team enterprise governance. No equivalent in AgentCore.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Memory stores turn-by-turn context within a session for multi-turn conversations without users repeating information.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry does not have a native managed memory/state-store product. "TrueMem" blog post describes a dual-memory concept but it is not a shipped product in the pricing or docs.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore-only. Use AgentCore Memory for agent short-term context management. TrueFoundry has no conflict here.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Memory automatically extracts user preferences / facts / session summaries and persists them across sessions. Shareable across agents in multi-agent systems.
TrueFoundry Description: No managed long-term memory product in TrueFoundry.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore-only. No overlap or conflict.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Runtime runs each agent session in an isolated microVM (dedicated CPU / memory / filesystem). Supports up to 8-hour long-running agents. Framework-agnostic (LangGraph / CrewAI / Strands / custom).
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry's deployment platform supports model serving and agent deployment on Kubernetes (auto-scaling) but it is a separate product layer — not a serverless-per-session microVM runtime.
Integration Recommendation: Different abstraction levels. AgentCore Runtime = per-session microVM isolation. TrueFoundry Deployment = Kubernetes pod-based persistent model/agent hosting. Complementary: TrueFoundry can host MCP servers and model endpoints; AgentCore Runtime executes agent sessions on top.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Runtime supports both HTTP SSE streaming and persistent WebSocket connections for real-time bidirectional agent communication.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry AI Gateway supports streaming LLM responses (SSE) for chat completions. WebSocket / bidirectional streaming not documented.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry covers LLM-level SSE streaming. AgentCore Runtime adds bidirectional WebSocket for the full agent session — different protocol scope.

AgentCore Description: Each agent session has an isolated filesystem. Files / packages / artifacts persist across session stop/resume within the same session lifecycle.
TrueFoundry Description: No per-session filesystem isolation in TrueFoundry's AI Gateway layer.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore Runtime advantage for stateful agent workflows requiring sandboxed file access.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Runtime can host and run stateful MCP servers as agent workloads — not just proxy to external ones.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry can deploy and host custom MCP servers as Kubernetes workloads behind the MCP Gateway.
Integration Recommendation: Both can host MCP servers. AgentCore's stateful MCP server hosting (per-session microVM) is stronger for ephemeral session-scoped tools; TrueFoundry's Kubernetes hosting is better for persistent shared MCP servers.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Runtime supports A2A protocol for inter-agent communication enabling multi-agent collaboration.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry Agent Gateway explicitly supports A2A protocol for inter-agent messaging and session-aware multi-agent orchestration.
Integration Recommendation: Both support A2A. If using both platforms for agent hosting the A2A protocol provides the integration bridge. Design so A2A spans both layers without creating routing loops.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Runtime supports AG-UI servers for agent-driven UI interactions.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry does not document AG-UI protocol support.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore-only at present.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Code Interpreter provides an isolated sandbox for agents to execute code enhancing accuracy for complex analytical tasks.
TrueFoundry Equivalent: Private Code Interpreter (blog post / not a shipping gateway feature)
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry blog references a "Private Code Interpreter" for in-VPC secure code execution but it is not a core AI Gateway product feature.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore Code Interpreter is a first-class service. TrueFoundry's code execution story is primarily self-hosted reference architecture. No direct conflict.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Browser provides a cloud-managed headless browser for agents to navigate websites / fill forms / extract data. Integrates with Playwright and BrowserUse.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry does not offer a managed browser / web automation service.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore-only. No TrueFoundry equivalent in the AI Gateway stack.

AgentCore Feature: AWS Agent Registry (agents / MCP servers / skills / custom resources)
AgentCore Description: Centralized catalog for discovering agents / MCP servers / tools / skills. Approval workflow for curation. Hybrid semantic + keyword search. Accessible via MCP endpoint. IAM or JWT auth.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry MCP Gateway includes a centralized registry for MCP servers with instant discovery. Supports publish and discovery for all registered servers.
Integration Recommendation: Both are discovery catalogs for MCP servers and tools. AWS Agent Registry is broader (agents + skills + custom resources + approval workflow); TrueFoundry MCP Registry is focused on MCP servers. If both are deployed use AWS Agent Registry as the enterprise-wide catalog and TrueFoundry Registry for real-time gateway-layer discovery.

AgentCore Description: AWS Agent Registry can register deployed AI agents as discoverable catalog resources across the organization.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry has a separate Agent Registry product under its Agent Platform for building / publishing / sharing AI agents.
Integration Recommendation: Conceptually equivalent — both catalog deployable agents. AWS Agent Registry integrates with AgentCore Runtime; TrueFoundry Agent Registry integrates with TrueFoundry's deployment platform. Pick one as your agent catalog per environment.

AgentCore Description: AWS Agent Registry supports agent skills as cataloged resources.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry Skills Registry stores versioned reusable SKILL.md instruction sets for agents and IDEs.
Integration Recommendation: Different abstraction: AWS skills = agent capabilities; TrueFoundry skills = prompt/instruction templates. Not conflicting.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Evaluations provides automated LLM-as-Judge evaluators (built-in and custom) on sessions / traces / spans from Strands / LangGraph agents. Supports online / on-demand / batch / dataset / simulation evaluation modes.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry does not have a native LLM-as-Judge evaluation pipeline. LangSmith integration is available for evaluation via TrueFoundry AI Gateway traces.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore Evaluations is the clear leader here. TrueFoundry can export traces to LangSmith for evaluation — those two are complementary. No direct TrueFoundry competitor.

AgentCore Description: Supports continuous online evaluation (production traffic sampling) and on-demand / batch evaluation modes.
TrueFoundry Description: N/A
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore-only. Critical for HIPAA-grade pre-deployment quality gates on prior-auth and claims agents.

AgentCore Description: Build and deploy custom LLM-as-Judge evaluators with private IAM resource policies.
TrueFoundry Description: N/A
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore-only.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore does not have a prompt versioning / management product.
TrueFoundry Description: Versioned prompt store with rollback / publishing / built-in playground. Supports A/B testing of prompt variants via virtual models.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry-only. Run TrueFoundry Prompt Management for all prompt lifecycle work — no conflict with AgentCore.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore Payments provides agent wallet management / configurable spend limits / x402 protocol for micro-payments to paid APIs / MCP servers.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry has no wallet or microtransaction billing layer.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore-only. Relevant if agents need to pay for third-party data services.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore inherits AWS compliance posture: SOC2 / HIPAA-eligible via AWS BAA / HITRUST through the AWS shared responsibility model.
TrueFoundry Equivalent: SOC2 Type 2 / HIPAA / ITAR / GDPR / FIPS (TrueFoundry platform certifications)
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry holds SOC2 Type 2 and is HIPAA / ITAR / GDPR / FIPS-certified as a platform. Supports air-gapped / on-prem / VPC deployments for full data residency.
Integration Recommendation: Both are HIPAA-eligible. AWS compliance is inherited; TrueFoundry's certifications are platform-level. For healthcare insurance workloads both BAAs are needed. TrueFoundry's on-prem / VPC option adds data residency flexibility that AgentCore (cloud-only) does not provide.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore is available only in supported AWS regions. No on-prem or hybrid deployment.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry can be deployed as SaaS / VPC-hosted / on-prem / air-gapped for maximum data sovereignty.
Integration Recommendation: For member PHI that cannot leave your data center TrueFoundry's on-prem gateway deployment is a significant differentiator over AgentCore.

AgentCore Description: AgentCore is configured via AWS Console / CLI / SDK — no YAML GitOps model documented.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry gateway and policy configuration is YAML-based and GitOps-compatible.
Integration Recommendation: TrueFoundry GitOps model enables infrastructure-as-code governance for HIPAA audit trails on configuration changes.

AgentCore Description: Single API call defines model + system prompt + tools; Harness handles orchestration / tool execution / memory / response generation. Each session in isolated microVM with filesystem.
TrueFoundry Description: TrueFoundry can deploy agents on Kubernetes but does not provide a managed single-API-call agent loop abstraction.
Integration Recommendation: AgentCore Harness is a unique capability for rapid single-agent deployment. No TrueFoundry equivalent in the AI Gateway layer.
